messages.subject: ggobi
parts:
Folks:
Maybe this is a better question for R-Digest but allow me to ask this
here.

What is ggobi and what does it offer? If I understand correctly, it
allows you to dynamically select a set of characteristic values and
look at data based on that. For example,

Product Customer Product Group Sales (this is
weekly sales, longitudinal data)
p1 c1 pg1 10
20 40 80 90 ...
p2 c1 pg1 16
26 46 88 99 ...
p2 c2 pg1 11
12 21 89 90 ...

Now if you want to select p2 and pg1, rows 2 and 3 will be added up
and shown to the user.

I am thinking it is something like the graphing that demand planning
software packages (the ones I know) like i2 DP or SAP APO DP do.

I may be totally wroong. Could you tell me what ggobi does (that
ggplot does not do and the caveat is mentioned in the first few pages
by Hadley in his pdf file that soon to be published).

Thanks.

Satish

messages.author: 52e73b2030a3e651
messages.subject: Re: ggobi
parts:
ggobi does tours and projection pursuit, for example 3D projections (principal coordinates plots of datasets, for example, automatically rotated by projection pursuit and scaled to emphasize contrasts between groups); also dynamic selection of the axes

Suppose that I think STRUCTURE is a piece of garbage and decide that sphered principal coordinates are good enough for me to represent the proportions of genetic ancestry in a large study.  (Wouldn't want to have our conclusions screwed up by "associating" a gene with a disease when that disease and that gene are, by coincidence, unusually well represented in a particular ethnic group or groups)  Ggobi is nice because you can monkey around with the data on the fly to determine which PCs cleanly separate which ethnic groups (e.g. Yorubans vs. everyone else) and additionally label points by their self-reported ethnicity, residence, whatever.  It's a great exploratory tool once you get used to it.

I like to use it for quality control in microarray studies, personally; once a sensible QA pipeline has been established, it's no longer an issue, but when gauging the effectiveness of automated QC or of metrics for the same, it's quite handy.

Try doing some of the examples, particularly with 2D and 2D+1D tours.  That's far better than any explanation I can write.

Hope this helps.


--t
